svg.text: Fig 12.2: application split into two segments
application part 2 (the library also grew near 70008)
Quirks of the era: programmers wrote the origin statement (in the PDP-8 example, *200 loads code at address 200 octal) because programs were not relocatable; the GETSTR
subroutine and a unit test were compiled with the library source as one program; the author's first employer kept several dozen decks of library source on a shelf; core
memory kept the loaded function library for days. Moore's law: speed, memory and density double every 18 months, true from the 1950s to 2000, then, for clock rates,
dynamically linked files that can be plugged together at runtime are the software components of our architectures (a Minecraft mod is a .jar in a folder; Resharper
plugs into Visual Studio as DLLs); it took 50 years, but a component plugin architecture can now be the casual default instead of a herculean effort
